items.title: Smooth projective analytifications have rational Kähler forms
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
Jacobian-criterion, ample-powers, Chern-form and comparison suppliers below.
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex scheme of pure dimension $n\ge0$.

Then the closed points of $X$ carry a structure of **complex manifold**
$X^{\mathrm{an}}$, its **analytification**: if $X\ne\varnothing$ and $n\ge1$
this is a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth complex manifold of complex
dimension $n$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]); if $n=0$ it is the
finite discrete set $X(\mathbb C)$ with its unique complex structure in the
convention of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]; and if
$X=\varnothing$ then $X^{\mathrm{an}}=\varnothing$. Every standard smooth
algebraic chart of $X$ becomes a holomorphic chart of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and
more generally, every morphism between smooth separated finite-type complex schemes of pure dimensions induces a holomorphic map between their analytifications. These analytifications are constructed by the same charts and need not be compact; separatedness and finite type ensure that they are Hausdorff and second-countable.

Moreover, for every ample invertible sheaf $A$ on $X$ there is a smooth
positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta_A$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ whose de Rham
class is the real image of the topological first Chern class
$c_1(A):=c_1(A^{\mathrm{an}})\in H^2(X^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Z)$:
$$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$
where $J$ is the de Rham comparison and $\rho$ the change of coefficients
$\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$
([[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]).
In dimension $n=0$ and for $X=\varnothing$ every $2$-form and every degree-two
cohomology class is zero and $\eta_A=0$, so the identity holds trivially.
items.strategy: All six proof steps and all nineteen actual dependency statements/definitions checked. Standard smooth presentations meet the exact implicit/inverse theorem dimension hypotheses; the zero-equation zero-dimensional chart is direct. Maximal residue fields give closed complex points, finite affine covers give a countable base, and the closed diagonal gives Hausdorffness. Projective topology and injective holomorphic differential follow from quotient presentations with regular free-coordinate lifts. FS overlap ratio h=Z_k/Z_j and O(1) metric weights psi_j=|Z_j/Z_k|^2 psi_k agree; Hermitian local connection curvature gives -Omega/(2 pi i)=omega_FS and pullback divides by positive d. Tensor additivity is licensed componentwise by numerability, CGWH and CW homotopy type. Checked X empty, n=0, r=0, N=0, positivity and class normalization; AC inherited from declared suppliers. Restricting functoriality to smooth separated finite-type schemes is necessary and retains projective/quasiprojective uses. Six reader-added supplier deps reconciled in owned manifest; no further item repair.

The chart construction and the Fubini-Study computation are elementary.

items.title: Kähler identities give Lefschetz sl-two and hard Lefschetz
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold with Kähler form
$\omega$, in the conventions of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], and put
$L=[\omega]\smile(-)$ on cohomology. Then the following hold.

- $L^{n-k}:H^k(X;\mathbb R)\to H^{2n-k}(X;\mathbb R)$ is an isomorphism for
  $0\le k\le n$.
- Harmonic representatives transport $(L,\Lambda,H)$ to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$
  action: $L$ is cup product with $[\omega]$, $\Lambda$ on cohomology means
  applying $\Lambda$ to the harmonic representative and not to an arbitrary
  closed form, $H$ acts by $\deg-n$, and
  $[L,\Lambda]=H$, $[H,L]=2L$, $[H,\Lambda]=-2\Lambda$ hold on cohomology.
- Primitive cohomology is
  $P^k=\{a\in H^k(X;\mathbb R):\text{the harmonic representative of }a\text{ lies in }\ker\Lambda\}$,
  and for $0\le k\le n$ one has
  $P^k=\ker\bigl(L^{n-k+1}:H^k(X;\mathbb R)\to H^{2n-k+2}(X;\mathbb R)\bigr)$;
  for every $k$,
  $$H^k(X;\mathbb R)=\bigoplus_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^rP^{k-2r},$$
  and a class of type $(p,q)$ has primitive components of type $(p-r,q-r)$.
- If $[\omega]$ is the real image of a rational class
  $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, all these decompositions and $L$-isomorphisms are
  rational, and they remain isomorphisms after extension to every
  characteristic-zero field.
items.strategy: Fixed-degree primitive projectors are rational polynomials in L,Lambda, so commuting with Delta makes the pointwise primitive components smooth harmonic forms; a merely pointwise decomposition was insufficient. Transport uses unique harmonic representatives, especially for Lambda, not arbitrary closed representatives. The finite strings give the isomorphism and both directions of the primitive-kernel characterization. Formula P^k=ker L^(n-k+1) is restricted to 0<=k<=n, with P^k=0 above n. Rational cup matrices invertible over R already invert over Q, and primitive direct sums/lowering coefficients remain rational over every characteristic-zero extension. Checked n=0, k=0,n, zero primitive spaces and complementary bounds; AC inherited from analytic/comparison suppliers. Source: Schnell Class 18, pp.4-5, Theorem 18.13 and Corollary 18.14; source typo in complex-vs-real seed wording is not adopted. Current producer findings 2,4,5 are independently resolved and refuter bound is immediate.

items.title: Morphisms, polarizability and simplicity of rational Hodge structures
items.statement: With the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], all structures in this item are rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight $k$. A **morphism of Hodge structures** $f:(V,\{V^{p,q}\})\to(W,\{W^{p,q}\})$ is a $\mathbb Q$-linear map $f:V\to W$ whose $\mathbb C$-linear extension satisfies $f_{\mathbb C}(V^{p,q})\subseteq W^{p,q}$ for all $p+q=k$. **Kernels and images** are again rational sub-Hodge structures: a bidegree-preserving map sends the bidegree components of a vector into the matching components, so $\ker(f_{\mathbb C})=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\bigl(\ker(f_{\mathbb C})\cap V^{p,q}\bigr)$ and $\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\bigl(\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})\cap W^{p,q}\bigr)$, the second sum being direct because the target bidegrees $W^{p,q}$ are distinct. The **direct sum** is $(V\oplus W)^{p,q}=V^{p,q}\oplus W^{p,q}$, with the inclusions and projections as morphisms. A **short exact sequence** $0\to U\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{\pi}W\to 0$ of weight-$k$ Hodge structures consists of morphisms that are exact as a sequence of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces; it **splits** in the category of Hodge structures if $\pi$ admits a morphism $s:W\to V$ with $\pi\circ s=\operatorname{id}_W$. A Hodge structure is **polarizable** if it admits a polarization, and **simple** if it has no nonzero proper rational sub-Hodge structure.
items.strategy: This item records the vocabulary invoked below on this page — the orthogonal splitting of polarized Hodge structures and the absolute projective Hodge package — as the pure weight-$k$ case of the morphisms of $\mathbb Q$-Hodge structures of Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.1.11)-(2.1.12), printed pp. 26-27. It is deliberately not routed through the mixed Hodge structures of a different page of this run, which lie outside this page's declared prerequisite closure. The only assertions to check are the componentwise closure claims recorded in the statement: if $x=\sum x^{p,q}$ and $f_{\mathbb C}(x)=0$, then $0=\sum f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ with $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})\in W^{p,q}$, so every $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$; and $\operatorname{im}(f_{\mathbb C})=\sum_{p+q=k}f_{\mathbb C}(V^{p,q})$ is direct because the target bidegrees are distinct. No proof phase applies to a definition, and no choice principle is used.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the item fixes definitions and verifies componentwise linear algebra; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Polarized rational Hodge structures split orthogonally
items.statement: Let $(V,Q)$ be a polarized rational pure Hodge structure and $U\subseteq V$ a rational sub-Hodge structure, with the notions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]] and [[def-morphisms-and-polarizability-of-rational-hodge-structures]]. Then $Q|_U$ is a polarization of $U$, and $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$ is an orthogonal direct sum of rational Hodge structures in which the complement is polarized. Every short exact sequence of polarizable rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight splits in the category of Hodge structures, and every polarizable rational pure Hodge structure is a finite direct sum of simple Hodge structures. These are claims about rational Hodge substructures; they do not assert a splitting for an arbitrary local system. Every rational splitting persists after extension of scalars to any characteristic-zero field; no positivity or ordered-field structure on that field is asserted, and a subobject over an extension field need not be defined over $\mathbb Q$.
items.strategy: Choice-free finite-dimensional linear algebra. Route: Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, (2.1.15)-(2.1.17), printed pp. 26-27, and Lemme (4.2.3) with its proof, printed p. 44. Step 1 (the restriction is a polarization). The Weil operator $C$ and complex conjugation preserve $U_{\mathbb C}$, because $U$ is a rational sub-Hodge structure. The form $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ restricts from $V$ to $U$, is positive definite there, and $Q|_U$ inherits rationality, $(-1)^k$-symmetry and type orthogonality from $Q$. If $u\in U$ lies in the radical of $Q|_U$, then $Cu$ does too: type orthogonality gives $Q(Cx,y)=Q(x,C^{-1}y)$ for all $x,y$, since both sides select the same $(p,q)$-$(q,p)$ components, so $Q(Cu,U)=Q(u,C^{-1}U)=0$. Then $h(u,u)=Q(Cu,\bar u)=0$, and positive definiteness forces $u=0$; hence $Q|_U$ is nondegenerate and is a polarization of $U$. Step 2 (the orthogonal complement). As $Q|_U$ is nondegenerate, the rational equations $Q(x,U)=0$ define a rational complement $U^{\perp_Q}$ with $\dim U^{\perp_Q}=\dim V-\dim U$ and $U\cap U^{\perp_Q}=0$, so $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$. If $x=\sum x^{p,q}\in U^{\perp_Q}_{\mathbb C}$ and $v\in U^{q,p}$, then $0=Q(x,v)=\sum_{r,s}Q(x^{r,s},v)=Q(x^{q,p},v)$, because $Q$ pairs $V^{r,s}$ nontrivially only with $V^{s,r}$; as $x^{q,p}$ pairs nontrivially only with type $(q,p)$, it is orthogonal to all of $U$. Thus each $x^{p,q}\in U^{\perp_Q}$, which is therefore a rational sub-Hodge structure, and the restriction of $h$ to it is positive definite; by Step 1 the restricted $Q$ is a polarization of the complement. Step 3 (splitting, semisimplicity, scalar extension). In a short exact sequence $0\to U\to V\to W\to 0$ of polarizable structures the middle term $V$ is polarizable; identify $U$ with its image, a rational sub-Hodge structure because a bidegree-preserving map has bidegree-preserving image and kernel, and fix a polarization $Q$ of $V$. By Step 2, $\pi$ restricts to an isomorphism $U^{\perp_Q}\to W$ of Hodge structures whose inverse is the required section, so the sequence splits. For semisimplicity, choose in a nonzero polarizable $V$ a nonzero rational sub-Hodge structure $U$ of least dimension; $U$ is simple, and $V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q}$ with polarizable complement of smaller dimension, so induction on $\dim V$ exhibits $V$ as a finite direct sum of simple structures. A rational splitting or direct-sum decomposition is given by rational matrices satisfying bidegree-wise linear identities (idempotence of the projections, and Q(x,U)=0 for the complement); these identities persist under scalar extension to any characteristic-zero field, so the splitting and the decomposition extend with it, and positivity is never invoked over that field.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the argument is finite-dimensional rational and complex linear algebra over fixed finite-dimensional structures; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations for smooth projective varieties
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold in the
conventions of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], with
Kähler form $\omega$, and let $0\le k\le n$. For this proof also write $Q_k$ for the same form on all of $H^k$, and on the primitive space $P^k$ put
$$Q_k(a,b)=\epsilon(k)\int_Xa\wedge b\wedge\omega^{n-k},$$
where $a,b$ are closed smooth representatives of the classes and the integral
is independent of the representatives. This form is $(-1)^k$-symmetric, pairs
$P^{p,q}$ only with $P^{q,p}$, and for nonzero $a\in P^{p,q}$ satisfies
$$i^{p-q}Q_k(a,\bar a)=(n-k)!\,\|a_{\mathrm{harm}}\|_{L^2}^2>0.$$
If $[\omega]=\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, then $Q_k$ is a rational polarization
of $P^k$, and full $H^k$ is polarized by the orthogonal direct sum form $S_k$
that on $L^rP^{k-2r}$ is $(-1)^rQ_k$, equivalently
$S_k(L^ru,L^rv)=Q_{k-2r}(u,v)$ for $u,v\in P^{k-2r}$; degrees $k>n$ are
polarized by transporting the polarization of $H^{2n-k}$ along $L^{k-n}$, with
Tate shift. For every real Kähler class the same positivity and nondegeneracy
statements hold, without rationality. In particular this applies to smooth
closed complex projective submanifolds of projective space with a hyperplane
polarization, hence to smooth projective complex varieties through their smooth
projective analytifications; more generally it applies to every real Kähler
class, including $\ell+\epsilon\eta$ when represented by a positive closed
form. For any continuous family of Kähler classes the primitive kernels (of
every fixed degree $0\le k\le n$) vary continuously as subspaces; rational
primitive spaces are asserted only at rational classes.
items.strategy: Stokes licenses independence of closed representatives; bidegree forces the complementary-type pairing. Weil on the conjugate primitive harmonic form gives i^(p-q)Q_k(a,bar a)=(n-k)! norm(a)^2; distinct types then give a positive Hermitian form and nondegeneracy. Real/complex top integration and the integral fundamental class license rationality; C preserves P_C, not necessarily P_Q. Q_k now explicitly has full H^k domain for its use on string summands; b_s has degree k-2s. Cross strings vanish because r<s puts at least n-(k-2r)+1 L factors on the harmonic primitive a_r; (-1)^r epsilon(k)=epsilon(k-2r) makes the block forms positive. Higher degrees transport through L^(k-n) with twist -(k-n), which raises weight to k and preserves C; k>2n gives the zero polarization. Kähler representatives of rational ample classes use the checked analytification supplier. Kernel matrices depend polynomially on continuous classes and have constant rank dim H^(k-2); a nonzero pivot minor proves local continuous kernel graphs without choosing continuous forms. Checked n=0,k=0,n, k>2n, zero primitive spaces, k=0,1 rank-zero maps and no positivity at non-Kähler limits. AC covers Stokes/analytic comparisons. No further item repair necessary.

items.title: Polarized Hodge and hard Lefschetz package for smooth projective varieties
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
suppliers below. For a smooth projective complex variety $X$ of pure dimension
$n$ with a chosen ample line class $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, its rational
cohomology is finite-dimensional pure Hodge in each degree, functorial for
pullback along holomorphic maps of the analytifications. Cup product has Hodge
type $(0,0)$ and $\ell$ has type $(1,1)$. For $0\le k\le n$ the
hard-Lefschetz maps $\ell^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ are rational isomorphisms,
and for $k>n$ so are the complementary maps $\ell^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$; the rational
primitive summands satisfy the Hodge–Riemann positivity of
[[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]], and
the sign-adjusted full cohomology pairing is a rational polarization. Rational
Hodge substructures split orthogonally. The same absolute positivity and
hard-Lefschetz statements hold for real Kähler classes, and primitive kernels
vary continuously along Kähler families. Rational splittings and isomorphisms
persist after extension to any characteristic-zero field. This package does
not supply weak hyperplane Lefschetz, relative hard Lefschetz, singular
intersection-cohomology purity, or semisimplicity of arbitrary local systems.
items.strategy: Analytification realizes the ample integral class by a positive closed (1,1)-form, Hodge comparison gives rational finite-dimensional pure cohomology, and harmonic Lefschetz supplies rational strings/isomorphisms. For n<k<=2n, ell^(k-n) is the forward hard-Lefschetz map in degree 2n-k, not the inverse of an incorrectly indexed map; its inverse is separately rational. For k>2n both source and target are zero. The signed orthogonal block polarizations imply nondegenerate Q_k, so precomposition by L^(n-k) proves nondegenerate complementary cup evaluation; transposition covers higher degree. Orthogonal Hodge splitting and rational identities extend to any characteristic-zero field, without positivity or simplicity claims there. Primitive continuity is restricted to fixed degrees along Kähler families. Empty, n=0,k=0,n, high-degree zero spaces checked. AC inherited exactly from suppliers; no relative, weak hyperplane, intersection-cohomology or arbitrary local-system conclusion is used. Added complementary-pairing derivation supports the actual middle-limit consumer F1 without an extra prerequisite.

items.title: Primitive one-forms and the Weil star sign
items.statement:
With the form-side conventions of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]: let $V$ be
the oriented Euclidean two-plane with positively oriented orthonormal basis
$e,f$, Kähler form $\omega=e\wedge f$, and compatible complex structure $J$,
acting by pullback on forms, with
$$Je=-f,\qquad Jf=e$$
(equivalently $f=-Je$). Then the type-$(1,0)$ form $u=e+if$ is primitive and
satisfies $*u=-iu$. Its positive norm density is
$$u\wedge*\bar u=2\,e\wedge f .$$
items.strategy: Choice-free two-plane verification: Ju=iu and Lambda u=0 by degree; the real complementary-basis star extends complex-linearly to *u=-iu and *bar(u)=i bar(u), so u wedge *bar(u)=2 e wedge f. This agrees with the primitive Weil formula at n=k=1. The Hermitian star identity conjugates its second argument.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: the verification is a finite-dimensional computation on a two-plane and consumes only the choice-free pointwise suppliers.
